scope: Formalize the supplied scalar Bernstein argument by elementary algebraic sign proofs, without changing the quartic or recomputing its Bernstein coefficients.
decisions: The current sources, entire available 19386-blob Lean archive and existing vendor OAI closure were searched. The 64 broad matches concern other uses of kappa, critical row phases or Karlsson quotient models; no scalar Bernstein or Sturm implementation was located.

CriticalScalarReduction is the existing p,J,W reduction, not the remaining quartic interval exclusion; CriticalScalarGaugeAlgebra changes Newton coordinates. Existing quartic variants supply factorization, not interval signs.

Reuse the current generic quartic definition and current modulus interval definitions and the supplied 25 factored Bernstein expressions. High131 is High013 in reverse order; avoid duplicated identities.

Only five higher-degree factors need new sign arguments. Use their supplied polynomials, algebraic shifts and Mathlib ring/positivity. This changes only the method of proving signs, not the quartic or allowed domain.
Keep endpoints k=1/3 and k=1 and the kappa=0 case explicit. No physical-to-quartic implication is claimed.

Use Mathlib Convex.mem_Icc directly for the interval argument. Four quartic interpolation identities cover five patches. The16distinct stored coefficient expressions share proofs; no root-count, gcd or root-isolation certificate is needed for the candidate implication.

A later targeted reuse review found that three local scalar helpers and the k=1 consumer overlapped CriticalModulusQuarticReal. The local proofs have been removed and the archive module is now directly imported, with imports changed only. The consolidated classification compiles and passes its14endpoint audit.
